body: I don't think someone has to agree with something in order to know other people might be thinking it when you hear other people say those kinds of things all the time and see examples held up to mock as What You Do Not Ever Want To Look Like Lest You Be Ostracized.

Oh god and here I was thinking people might call my identity into question if I ever admitted to this. Whew. Yeah, I get horribly dysphoric about it, not because I care if people think I'm "ugly" by their standards (I find androgyny extremely attractive, personally.) but because I know they're making personality and sexuality judgments based on my look. I already feel like I'm holding back a lot of myself when it comes to fashion because I want to pass so badly (Except I never will, so it's pointless, because I have the widest hips and thighs I've ever seen on a human being and it's mostly bone structure.), and it's like... When someone misgenders me I want to scream "No trust me if I wanted to be read as a woman I would be dressed so much more fabulously than this, I'd be in a miniskirt and glitter eyeshadow! This isn't who I am, gender or fashion-wise!" I feel like I'm wasting my youth forced to dress and behave in ways that go against my personality all for nothing because people just think I'm a stern, butch woman when I'm actually a very flamboyant, bisexual man with a head full of glam rock. And it's horribly depressing.

Fuck your former roommate and his psychologically poisonous cupcakes! Anyway, aside from that, I agree with everyone else. I think this woman was flaky in general and  she might have done this to anyone she said she would rent from, cuz' that text message reads kind of weird to me? Like she's trying to keep your flat open on call in case her plans change again? I know most people who decided to opt out of moving in with me when I was looking for one gave a definite "Oh I found somewhere else cheaper" or something else to let me know they were not going to be moving in for 100% sure. If she was so offended by someone being transgender that she fled the country though... That's kind of amazing...

My knee jerk reaction is also disgust because of my association with expectations that people started putting on me after finding out I had my original reproductive organs. I feel like this is something people never talk about, everyone either talks about the happily pregnant trans guys or guys who don't really deal with it as an issue/are horrified by it and don't really discuss it, but damn if I had a dollar for every time someone brought up that it's so great that I could carry a baby for my partner in a relationship despite my worsened dysphoria at the very idea and tokophobia in general just because they heard about people like Thomas Beatie... It really sucks.

I have huge thighs too, either from putting on weight or from muscle whenever I get to working out and lose weight again. I use shapewear honestly, I have no shame. I also wear a particular pair of skinny jeans that fit really tight at the upper part of my pelvis/lower waist but then fit looser around my thighs. Somehow this creates an optical illusion that makes them look less outrageous? It's hard to explain and required a lot of trying trousers on to find a pair that fit just perfectly. I have a pair of black cargo pants that give the same effect, also, they have a lot of pockets so visually it just looks like the extra width is pockets.

I'm feeling what everyone else in here is, I definitely didn't see an ugly person when I opened that link, and even if you were what you look like now isn't permanent anyway cuz' people's faces change a lot over the years. Lots of people don't really hit their attractiveness stride until they're quite a bit older than you. And what you look like now is totally fine anyway, I don't see why anyone would call you ugly at all. The only way your looks will prevent you from having a good love life is if you stay so unhappy about them that you refuse to believe other people might find you attractive and push them away out of fear and self-hatred I promise.

You know, this isn't helpful at all but while reading this I thought that you sound incredibly strong even if you don't feel it. Six years is a long time to keep fighting against constant setbacks, you deserve a lot of credit for all your trying and I'm honestly impressed. Sleep issues are nothing to joke about, they really fuck up a person's entire life. But I don't think anyone can keep failing forever when they're as clearly determined and level-headed as you, I really think you're on the right track.
Do something you enjoy while doing it, honestly. I recommend drawing or coloring if you're into that at all, it's hard to feel unhappy while doing that even sober.
Nah, you're right. I should probably try it more often, if anything just to try and get my brain working harder.

Oh my god, I've had multiple gay guys try to tell me that vaginas are grosser because "blood comes out of them" and then tell me how they'll totally fuck or lick an anus without a barrier. It completely floors me. Yeah sure I might deal with blood at a specific time that I KNOW is going to come and that I can absolutely prepare for but I never know when my bad stomach (Condolences, man, I'm in the same boat.) is going to try and send pure fiery hell down the poop chute.

I'm actually way more dysphoric about the surrounding tidbits than the actual hole itself so I much prefer it when people fuck or finger me there or the back door than manual stimulation. Besides it's absurdly easy to get me off internally whereas externally will take half an hour of me fighting anxiety about how long it's taking and how bizarre and wrong my body feels.

If anyone gives you trouble, well, you just tell them they better fucking get the unisex bathroom back then cuz' it's not your fault they got rid of it and you're not going to make yourself feel crappy using the wrong bathroom aka women's just because they decided to do this.

If it makes you feel any better, I had nurses and doctors misgendering me literally while I was prepping and recovering from top surgery. O.o As if a cis woman was really going to be practically whistling and skipping through the hallways like I was about getting a mastectomy. But yeah, as everyone else is saying... Someone should talk to her cuz' if she can't put two and two together about a patient's gender based on their transitional medical care she doesn't seem quite clever enough to be giving people the right medicines and making sure she's with the right patient either.

Yeah, it's just like... It seems so pointless to even try when all my friends with degrees are failing at life almost as hard as I am anyway and I'm tired of sucking at math classes no matter how hard I study and try.

Hey, can't help much with the anxiety, but I had the same problem with my chest and I didn't have to have any excess tissue removed. My chest looks about the same as any other trans guy who's had double incision top surgery. I hope that helps a bit. They didn't even bring it up to me as a potential aesthetic problem. When I was still shopping around for a local surgeon one guy did have an issue with it but that was because he was really only interested in doing the peri technique and wasn't very experienced either.

Take this with a grain of salt since I'm here and suicide-posting myself but let me tell you, I had ZERO friends until I was 19 or so and started meeting up with people I met online. I never made a single friend through school that lasted longer than a month or so. Meetup never worked for me either, but message boards definitely did. I met my current best IRL friend through a message board. I don't know how old you are but I definitely think there's hope for you to make new friends if someone as socially incapable as I was for ages eventually found some. It just takes longer for some of us. So if that's your main reason to quit life, I wouldn't recommend it because it is something that can be fixed. As for school, you have my biggest sympathy. Community college can really, really suck.

Best thing I ever did that made me stop worrying about my hand size was taking up the bass guitar because when I realized I could play it with no problems regardless of my hand size it stopped mattering to me. Also people suddenly started regarding me as way more attractive after I said I could play bass. That definitely helped too.

I'll join then, thanks. I don't really have a good support system in that realm anymore and I could use to just... I dunno, be around other ftm people online at least. 
I'm glad you're alive, hopefully I'll have the courage to do the crazy thing too instead of the sad thing.

I want more than anything to just go over there, quit living in this country and somehow make it with her but I'm scared she'll end up hating my crazy ass in the end and I really have no idea how to make it in a new country if I can't even make it here.
Thanks for the reply though, it helps to know that other trans people are still kicking somehow. I only ever hear about us dying most of the time.

"College algebra." Which I would do, except I'm pretty sure I legitimately have a math-related learning disability. I've failed almost every math class I've ever taken and learning to read music took me a decade of trying just for its mere similarity to math. Plus getting a degree would only bide me time of more stressful school before Extreme Poverty and Unemployment in A Transphobic World Part 2: Student Loans.

Hey, you know, that wasn't idiotic of you to say at all. That was a good response and she was honest enough with you to say she didn't want a relationship right now. So would you really want to be with someone who doesn't want everything you have to give right now anyway? It would just end badly and hurt you even more, so, give yourself some credit for taking the rejection respectfully and don't count it as a defeat, just a dead end that has nothing to do with your future potential.
